issues.description: The UML/problem statement declares a Pneumatic interface method named openValve(), but the solution implementation declares releaseValve() instead. This name/signature mismatch between the specification and the solution will confuse students and cause inconsistencies when they implement or compare against the reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the method in the solution (and any reference implementations) from releaseValve() to openValve() so the Pneumatic interface matches the UML/problem statement. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use releaseValve() if that name is intentional. Ensure template, tests, and solution use the same method name.

issues.description: The Pneumatic interface method name in the problem statement (openValve) does not match the method name in the solution (releaseValve). This creates a direct mapping/confusion for students: the UML and problem ask for openValve(), while the solution defines releaseValve() and the implementing classes override openValve(). The mismatch breaks the conceptual mapping and will cause compilation/expectation confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method name across artifacts. Rename releaseValve() in the solution Pneumatic interface to openValve(), and update all implementing classes to override openValve(). Alternatively, update the problem/UML to use releaseValve() consistently if that name was intended.
